This appeal having been heard and reserved for order, co  pronouncement this day, the court passed the following:

ORDER This misc. appeal has been filed by appellants (hereinafter referred to as "respondents no.1 and 2")
who are the driver and the owner of the vehicle, involved in the accident, to challenge the award passed on03.12.2014 by Additional Member to Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mauganj District Rewa in Claim Case No.115/2013.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mauganj District Rewa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By that award, compensation amount of Rs.29,58,865/- was allowed in favour of respondents no.1 -3 (hereinafter referred to as 'claimants') and by fixing the liability to pay that amount jointly and severally upon respondents no.1 and 2, the insurance company (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no.3') was completely exonerated from the liability to pay the compensation amount.

2. Relevant facts for decision of this misc. appeal are in brief that Badri Prasad Sharma was injured in an accident, which was the result of rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no.1/ the driver of the tractor that was owned by respondent no.2.
Badri Prasad Sharma received treatments in different hospitals but he succumbed to his injuries in Jeevan Jyoti Hospital, Allahabad.
A criminal case was registered against respondent no.1.

Claimants are the wife and sons of Badri Prasad Sharma; they filed the claim petition for seeking compensation amount of more than Rs.33,00,000/-, which was partly allowed against respondents no.1 and 2, and respondent no.3 was completely exonerated from its liability on the ground that the vehicle was not insured at the time of accident.

3. The grounds raised in this misc. appeal by respondents no.1 and 2 are that the learned Tribunal failed to appreciate that vehicle in question was not involved in accident as it was engaged at that time in the agricultural field of Babulal Tiwari to accomplish a farming task therein; the FIR was made with a considerable delay; the statements of witnesses including Santosh Kumar Kol (PW/2)
were recorded with an exceptional delay and his statements were highly contradictory; the relevant witness was Mohd. Kuddus, but he was not examined before the Tribunal; it was Mohd. Kuddus Ansari who got the FIR lodged and the number of vehicle involved in the accident was not disclosed therein.
The Tribunal also erred in assessment of compensation amount.
There was no rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no.1.

The tractor was purchased under hire purchase Rakesh Pratap Singh vs Smt. Pushpa Sharma on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58729175/
2 agreement and its installment and also the premium to insurance company were also being paid regularly.

entities.text: Rakesh Pratap Singh vs Smt. Pushpa Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The premium was paid even prior to the date of accident, but the learned Tribunal failed to appreciate this fact and wrongly held that the vehicle was not insured on the date of accident, it is therefore prayed that the award be set aside and finding of fastening liability only upon respondents no.1 and 2 be set aside.
4.
Arguments of both the parties except the insurance company were heard on merits.

Though none appeared on behalf of insurance company to oppose the appeal, but written arguments on behalf of it have already been placed on record hence, they too need to be considered.
5.

The issue raised herein that needs to be decided fore-mostly is whether the offending vehicle was insured on the date of accident, i.e. 21.10.2012 and whether the learned Tribunal committed error in exonerating the insurance company from its liability.

It is pleaded in this context that at the time of accident, the insurance company was not running any office in Tahsil Hanumana District Rewa; it had authorized the branch of Union Bank of India operating in Tahsil Hanumana to collect premium amount of policy and to send the collected money to the office of insurance company.
This fact has been admitted by the office head of branch Rewa of insurance company namely Ratan Kumar (NAW/1) and also the clerk working in that office namely Kamta Prasad Kol (NAW/2).
Respondent no.2 himself appeared in witness box as NAW/3 and stated these facts on oath.

B.K.
Mitra (NAW/4) was the Branch Manager of Union Bank of India, Branch Hanumana District Rewa and during his examination, he has confirmed these facts.

6. It is, therefore, established that insurance company having no branch in Hanumana had authorized the Union Bank of India Branch Hanumana to receive collections against premium amount of policy and under this authority Union Bank of India had received the premium amount of insurance policy from respondent no.2.

The date of receiving this amount is although not proved by any entry made in ledger books of the bank, but certificate of D5 issued by B.K. Mitra (NAW/4)
suggests that this premium amount was received in the branch of the bank on 17.10.2012.

The same fact has also been admitted by the branch head of the insurance company Ratan Kumar (NAW1)
during his cross-examination.

7. On the basis of these material and unrebutted pieces of evidence, it is established that the premium amount against the insurance policy in question was received by authorized agent on 17.10.2022, however, the policy was issued on 26.10.2012.
This policy is Ex.D/2 and the earlier policy has been marked as Ex.D/1.
The earlier policy had expired on 13.10.2012 and the accident occurred between these two material dates, i.e. 13.10.2012 and 26.10.2012 as the date of accident was 21.10.2012.
The question arises whether under the insurance policy of Ex.D/2 for which the premium was received on 17.10.2012 the insurance company was liable to indemnify the insured.
8. The answer to above question lies in the provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 itself.
Under Section 145-A of Motor Vehicle Act "an authorized insurer means an insurer for the time being carrying on general insurance business in India ...................."

Section 145-B defines certificate of insurance, meaning thereby "a certificate issued by authorized insurer in pursuance of sub-section 3 of Section 147 of the Act and includes a cover- note complying with such requirement as may be Rakesh Pratap Singh vs Smt. Pushpa Sharma on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58729175/
3 prescribed and where more than one certificate has been issued in connection with a policy or where a copy of a certificate has been issued, all those certificates or that copy as the case may be."
9.

entities.text: Rakesh Pratap Singh vs Smt. Pushpa Sharma on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, Section 145-D declares that "policy of insurance includes certificate of insurance."
Section 146 of the Act stipulates that "no person shall use or allow any person to use a motor vehicle in public unless he has a policy of insurance complying with the requirements of the Act."

These sections very clearly establish that a vehicle cannot ply on a public road unless it has a policy of insurance complying with the requirements of the Act and policy of insurance includes certificate of insurance and even a cover-note.
But here, the respondent no.2 had none.
He had simply made payment of premium and without obtaining a cover-note or a certificate of insurance or an insurance policy he allowed his vehicle to be used in public.

10. Further, Section 147(3) of the Motor Vehicle Act reads that "a policy shall be of no effect for the purposes of this Chapter unless and until that is issued by an insurer in favour of the person by whom the policy is effected, a certificate of insurance in the prescribed form and containing the prescribed particulars of any condition subject to which the policy is issued......."
This shows that for making the insurer liable, there must be at least a cover-note even if the insurance policy is not immediately issued.
Without a cover-note/certificate of insurance, an insurance policy is not effective.

11. As the facts of the case disclose, the respondent no.2 was not having any cover note or certificate of insurance or an insurance policy therefore, premium paid on 17.10.2022 would itself not make an insurance policy operational or effective from that date.
Accordingly, it is held that the learned Tribunal committed no error in exonerating the insurance company from its liability as the insurance policy was not effective on the date of accident.

12. There is an I.A. No.2178/2016 pending for decision in the case, in which a prayer has been made to implead Union Bank of India Branch Hanumana as respondent no.5, but merely for the reason that the premium was collected by that Branch the status of bank cannot be considered as of a necessary party for the decision of this appeal hence, the prayer made therein cannot be allowed and accordingly, the application under consideration, for which it was observed in order dated 25.01.2017 that it shall be decided at the time of final hearing, is dismissed on merits.

entities.text: Union Bank of India Branch Hanumana
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 13. The other grounds raised herein is that the offending vehicle of the ownership of respondent no.2 was falsely implicated in the case.

It is claimed by respondents no.1 and 2 that on the date of accident the vehicle was engaged in the agricultural work in the field of Babulal Mishra and was not plying on the road where the alleged accident occurred.

To prove this fact, respondent no.2 Yagyabhan Singh has examined himself as NAW/3, but from his statements it appears that he himself was not with the vehicle at the time of alleged accident and admittedly respondent no.1 Rakesh Pratap Singh was its driver.
Therefore, the relevant testimony to prove this fact would have been of Rakesh Pratap Singh, i.e. the driver of the vehicle, but he has not been examined in the case.
Further, the respondents no.1 and 2 have failed to examine Babulal Mishra as witness in whose agricultural field the tractor was employed on the date of accident.

Although his affidavit has been filed but that could not have been considered on merits unless testator appeared before the Tribunal Rakesh Pratap Singh vs Smt. Pushpa Sharma on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58729175/
4 to verify its facts on oath.

entities.text: Tribunal Rakesh Pratap Singh vs Smt. Pushpa Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. The impugned award has also been challenged on the aspect of assessment of compensation.

It is proved before the tribunal that the deceased was working as Assistant Grade II employee in a Govt.
School who was aged between 47-48 years and was earning Rs.21084/- per month just prior to the accident.
The future prospects @ 30% were added to it and it was found that the wife and the two children aged 25 years and 16 years were dependent on the deceased.

It is claimed here by the respondents no.1 and 2 that the future prospects were wrongly added and dependency of elder son was also wrongly admitted, but there is no evidence on record to suggest that the elder son was employed and had started earning before the death of his father.
Further, the addition of future prospects is in conformity with the established legal principles.
Therefore, the impugned award cannot be assailed on these grounds as well.

15. On the basis of overall appreciation of facts and evidence, this misc. appeal is found to be devoid of any merits and is accordingly dismissed.
16.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the Tribunal alongwith record for information and necessary compliance.
